It starts with one ordinary video of a person dancing.
From that video alone, the program rebuilds the dancer in 3D: seventy-six joints, measured in metres, with both feet on the floor.
Every joint becomes a curve over time. This is the dance, as data.
It ran on fifteen dances in a row. Forty-nine minutes, with nobody touching it.

Two dancers work the same way. Each one becomes a colour-coded figure in one shared 3D room.
Both characters and the room are painted in a single pass, so they stay in step, in place, and in the same light.
